title: econ-lighthouse: automatic unit-econ projections and quant-profile annotator
author: Maya Ortega
description:
Context and motivation: We need better tenant-level cost recommendations that combine realistic unit-econ projections with quantization safety margins. Current defaults are conservative and require manual tuning. This PR introduces 'econ-lighthouse' — an automation that (a) synthesizes simulated unit-econ projections for a tenant/profile using sampled telemetry, (b) annotates and proposes quantization profiles with estimated quality delta, and (c) exposes a dry-run CLI and telemetry so operators can validate before rollout. Goals: reduce manual tuning time, provide explainable projections, and allow safe opt-in profile suggestions.

What this PR does (single-line summary): Adds an economics projection pipeline + quant-profile annotator, a dry-run CLI, model/tenant feature-flag gating, new telemetry metrics, and a small runtime fallback for conservative application.

Implementation notes: The projection engine (pkg/econ/projection) consumes sampled traces and historical latency/cost buckets to simulate per-token cost under different batching and quant profiles. The quant-profile annotator (pkg/quant/annotator) runs lightweight fuzz tests against a golden subset (5 prompt families) and produces an annotated profile: {profile_id, expected_cost_delta, median_quality_delta, regression_risk_score}. All heavy simulation runs are CPU-bound and scheduled on the existing autoscaler job queue; a short-circuit fast-path returns approximations for interactive dry-runs.

CLI and operator UX: new command 'rw econ inspect --tenant <id> --dry-run --profile-candidates smallfp16,int8-q4' produces a JSON report and summary table. The report includes a deterministic seed so results are reproducible and an explain block that maps the dominant cost drivers (batch shape, prefix reuse, kv-hit-rate). The CLI also supports '--apply=preview' to annotate tenant defaults in the Console without activating them.

Telemetry & observability: Adds metrics 'econ.projection.cost_estimated', 'econ.projection.quality_delta_p50', 'econ.annotator.regression_risk' and a Console dashboard template under Observability -> Economics (prefill). Traces include sampling tags to correlate with existing 'prefill' and 'batching' spans.

Safety and rollout: Feature-gated by tenant flag 'econ_lighthouse_v1'. Default behavior for non-opted tenants is unchanged. For opt-in tenants we create a Console preview and a gradual rollout that starts as a suggestion (no auto-apply) and can be promoted after manual QA. We built a fallback so if the annotator reports regression_risk > 0.12 we keep the tenant on existing profile.

Testing: unit tests for projection math (pkg/econ/projection/*_test.go), integration test that runs a dry-run against a recorded tenant trace (ci/integration/econ_dryrun.sh), and a small E2E smoke test in perf-canary that verifies CLI output shape. Performance: simulated workloads (internal perf harness) show a median simulated per-token cost reduction of 9.7% when applying suggested profiles for high-prefill workloads; median quality delta stays within 1.8 BLEU-equivalent units on our evaluation prompts.

Checklist:
- [x] Projection engine implementation and API
- [x] Quant-profile annotator with golden prompt check
- [x] Dry-run CLI and JSON report output
- [x] Telemetry metrics and Console dashboard template
- [x] Unit/integration tests and CI job
- [x] Feature flag + safe fallback
- [ ] Long-running tenant canary (follow-up ticket created)

Backward compatibility and risk: No changes to existing runtime behavior unless tenant enables the feature. Annotated profiles are suggestions by default; the apply path is opt-in. The main risk is false-negative regression_risk estimates for rare prompt families; we mitigated by conservative thresholds and requiring manual promotion for now.

Follow-ups: ENG-2319 track canary rollout and long-running validation; ENG-2410 introduce automated A/B quality checks for promoted profiles.

Related: references to prior heuristics work and prefilling telemetry (internal docs link: https://intranet.redwood/econ-lighthouse)
